title: XR Right Hip and Femur
author: Radiology Service
summary: Right intertrochanteric femur fracture with underlying osteopenia.
body:
**Exam**
XR right hip, AP pelvis and cross-table lateral, and XR right femur AP and lateral. Performed 11/07 at 2245.

**Indication**
Fall onto the right hip, shortened and externally rotated right leg, pain 8/10.

**Comparison**
None available.

**Findings**
- There is an acute, mildly displaced and comminuted fracture through the right intertrochanteric region with varus angulation of the proximal fragment and some posteromedial comminution involving the lesser trochanter.
- The femoral head remains seated in the acetabulum. No dislocation. The femoral neck and the remainder of the femoral shaft are intact on the dedicated femur views.
- Diffuse decreased bone mineralization consistent with osteopenia.
- The pelvis, pubic rami and left hip are intact. Mild degenerative changes of both hips. Soft tissues show expected swelling around the right proximal thigh.

**Impression**
1. Acute right intertrochanteric femur fracture, mildly displaced, with varus angulation and lesser trochanter involvement.
2. Osteopenia.
3. No additional acute fracture of the pelvis or femoral shaft.

Findings communicated to the ED provider at the time of the study.
impression: Acute right intertrochanteric femur fracture, mildly displaced with varus angulation. Osteopenia. No other acute pelvic or femoral fracture.

title: XR Chest Single View
author: Radiology Service
summary: Clear lungs with mild cardiomegaly and no acute cardiopulmonary disease.
body:
**Exam**
Portable AP chest radiograph, performed 11/07 at 2300.

**Indication**
Preoperative evaluation, hip fracture, age 82.

**Comparison**
None available.

**Findings**
- Lungs are clear. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
- Mild cardiomegaly. Mediastinal contour is normal for technique, with mild aortic tortuosity.
- No pulmonary vascular congestion or edema.
- Visualized bones show diffuse osteopenia without acute rib or shoulder fracture. Leads and monitoring wires are in place.

**Impression**
1. No acute cardiopulmonary disease.
2. Mild cardiomegaly.
impression: No acute cardiopulmonary disease. Mild cardiomegaly.

title: ED Provider Note - Right Hip Fracture
author: M. Castellano, MD
summary: 82-year-old woman with a mechanical fall and right intertrochanteric hip fracture, nerve block placed, Foley placed for retention, admitted to orthopedics.
body:
**Chief Complaint**
Fall at home with right hip pain, unable to bear weight.

**HPI**
82-year-old woman who tripped on a rug at home at about 2130 on 11/07 and fell onto her right hip. No head strike, no loss of consciousness, no preceding chest pain, palpitations, dizziness or syncope per patient; the fall was mechanical. She could not stand afterward and was brought in by EMS, arriving at 2215. Pain 8/10 at the right hip and groin, worse with any movement. She takes no anticoagulants.

**PMH / Medications / Allergies**
- Hypertension (lisinopril 10 mg daily), type 2 diabetes (metformin 500 mg BID, A1c 7.2%), CKD stage 3a (baseline creatinine 1.2), hypothyroidism (levothyroxine 75 mcg), osteoporosis (alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium and vitamin D), hyperlipidemia (atorvastatin 20 mg). No dementia.
- Allergy: sulfa antibiotics (rash).
- Never smoker, no alcohol. Lives alone, independent, uses a cane. Daughter Karen Mills is her health care proxy.

**Exam**
- 2215 vitals: T 98.4 F, HR 98, BP 158/88, RR 18, SpO2 95% on room air, pain 8/10. Weight 61 kg.
- Elderly woman in moderate discomfort, alert and oriented x4. Head atraumatic, cervical spine nontender, lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen soft and nontender, pelvis stable.
- Right leg shortened and externally rotated, tender over the greater trochanter, pain with log roll. Right foot warm, DP and PT pulses palpable, capillary refill under 2 seconds, sensation and toe movement intact. Left leg, wrists and spine without tenderness.

**ED Course**
- Fentanyl 25 mcg IV at 2235 with partial relief. After this she could not void and had suprapubic fullness; bladder scan 620 mL. Retention attributed to pain, opioid and immobility. A 16 Fr Foley was placed at 2330 with sterile technique and drained clear yellow urine. UA from the new catheter at 2340 was negative (clear, nitrite negative, leukocyte esterase negative, trace blood, WBC 0-2/hpf, no bacteria).
- Ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca nerve block at 2345 with ropivacaine 0.25% 30 mL; she tolerated it well and pain is improving. Neurovascular exam unchanged afterward.

**Results**
- X-ray right hip and femur: right intertrochanteric femur fracture with osteopenia. Chest x-ray: clear lungs, mild cardiomegaly, no acute disease.
- Labs 2230: WBC 8.4, Hgb 11.8, Hct 35.4, platelets 232, Na 138, K 4.2, CO2 25, BUN 22, creatinine 1.2 (eGFR 46), glucose 168, calcium 9.0, INR 1.0, troponin I 0.01 (negative). Type and screen A positive, antibody screen negative.
- ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute ischemic changes.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. Right intertrochanteric femur fracture after mechanical fall. Dr. Reyes (Orthopedics) consulted by phone, agrees with operative fixation; admit to orthopedics with hospital medicine co-management (Dr. Patel). NPO after midnight pending the admitting team, fall precautions.
2. Pain: acetaminophen scheduled, low-dose oxycodone PRN, avoid NSAIDs (CKD).
3. Urinary retention: Foley in place, strict I&O. Baseline UA negative.
4. Hold lisinopril and metformin on admission.

**Disposition**
Admit. Daughter updated at the bedside.

title: Orthopedic and Hospitalist Admission H&P
author: A. Reyes, MD; S. Patel, MD (co-management)
summary: 82-year-old woman admitted with a right intertrochanteric hip fracture for surgical fixation with medicine co-management.
body:
**Chief Complaint**
Right hip pain after a fall.

**History of Present Illness**
Doris Kowalczyk is an 82-year-old woman who tripped on a rug at home at about 2130 on 11/07 and fell onto her right hip. No head strike or loss of consciousness, no prodrome. She could not bear weight and was brought by EMS, arriving in the ED at 2215 with pain 8/10. X-ray showed a right intertrochanteric femur fracture. She received fentanyl 25 mcg IV and a fascia iliaca nerve block (2345) with good pain relief. She could not void after the opioid; bladder scan 620 mL and a 16 Fr Foley was placed at 2330. The UA from the new catheter at 2340 was negative. She is admitted to Orthopedics with hospital medicine co-management.

**Past Medical History**
Hypertension; type 2 diabetes (A1c 7.2%); CKD stage 3a (creatinine 1.2, eGFR about 45); hypothyroidism; osteoporosis; hyperlipidemia. No history of CAD, stroke, DVT/PE or dementia. Surgical history not significant for anesthetic problems.

**Home Medications**
Lisinopril 10 mg daily; metformin 500 mg BID; levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; alendronate 70 mg weekly; calcium carbonate 500 mg with vitamin D 400 units BID; atorvastatin 20 mg nightly. No anticoagulants or antiplatelets.

**Allergies**
Sulfa antibiotics (rash).

**Social / Functional**
Widow, lives alone in a two-story house (bedroom upstairs). Independent in ADLs, drives, uses a cane. Never smoker, no alcohol. Wears glasses and a left hearing aid. Daughter Karen Mills (health care proxy) lives 20 minutes away. Goal is to return home. Full Code.

**Review of Systems**
Positive for right hip pain. Negative for chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, fever, cough, dysuria, headache or focal weakness.

**Physical Exam**
- Vitals 2330: T 98.4 F, HR 96, BP 150/84, RR 18, SpO2 96% on room air, pain 7/10. Height 160 cm, weight 61 kg, BMI 23.8.
- Comfortable at rest, alert and oriented x4, hearing aid on. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender; Foley in place draining clear yellow urine.
- Right leg shortened and externally rotated, thigh swollen with no tense compartment. DP and PT pulses palpable, capillary refill under 2 s, sensation and toe movement intact. Left leg normal.

**Data**
WBC 8.4, Hgb 11.8, platelets 232, Na 138, K 4.2, BUN 22, creatinine 1.2, glucose 168, INR 1.0, troponin negative. ECG sinus rhythm. Chest x-ray clear with mild cardiomegaly. Hip x-ray: right intertrochanteric fracture, osteopenia.

**Assessment**
82-year-old woman with a right intertrochanteric femur fracture, medically optimized for surgery with an elevated but acceptable risk given age, diabetes, hypertension and CKD 3a.

**Plan**
1. Fracture: operative fixation (cephalomedullary nail) within 24-36 hours, tentatively Sunday afternoon. NPO after 0600 except sips with medications. Consent with patient and Karen. Perioperative cefazolin 2 g IV x3 doses.
2. Pain: acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO q8h scheduled, oxycodone 2.5-5 mg PO q4h PRN, bowel regimen. No NSAIDs (CKD).
3. VTE: SCD on the left leg; enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily to start after surgery when hemostasis allows (CrCl about 35 mL/min, dose acceptable).
4. Hypertension / diabetes / CKD: hold lisinopril and metformin (NPO, surgery, CKD). Insulin lispro correction scale AC and HS. Continue levothyroxine and atorvastatin; hold alendronate. Strict I&O, BMP and CBC in the morning.
5. Foley: placed in the ED for urinary retention (bladder scan 620 mL). Recommend removal in the morning if possible; bladder scan if she cannot void.
6. Delirium and fall prevention: glasses and hearing aid on, bed alarm, avoid benzodiazepines.
7. Type and screen on file. Full Code.

title: Anesthesia Record Summary
author: K. Lindqvist, MD
summary: Spinal anesthesia for right hip fixation, hemodynamics managed with phenylephrine and LR, EBL 350 mL, to PACU.
body:
**Anesthesia Record Summary**
Procedure: ORIF right intertrochanteric femur fracture. ASA class III. Anesthesia start 1410, surgery 1430-1615.

**Preoperative**
82-year-old, 61 kg, HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a. NPO after 0600. Preoperative vitals 1345: T 98.4 F, HR 80, BP 140/78, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air. Hgb 11.4 (0600), creatinine 1.1. Lisinopril and metformin held. Cefazolin 2 g IV at 1400.

**Technique**
Spinal anesthesia at L3-4 in the sitting position, 25 g pencil-point needle, first pass, with hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.5% 10 mg. Sensory level T10. Light propofol sedation at 20-30 mcg/kg/min. Oxygen 2 L/min by nasal cannula. Standard ASA monitors.

**Hemodynamics**
- Baseline BP 140/78, HR 80. After spinal onset BP fell to a nadir of 90/50 (MAP 63) about 15 minutes into positioning, treated with phenylephrine 100 mcg IV x3 and a fluid bolus, with a good response.
- Intraoperative range: SBP 92-125, HR 78-96, SpO2 95-100%, no arrhythmia.
- At transfer to PACU: BP 96/54, HR 104, SpO2 95% on 3 L nasal cannula. Mildly low and heart rate rising; flagged to PACU for close recheck, STAT CBC and a fluid bolus if BP does not recover.

**Fluids / Blood Loss**
- Lactated Ringer's 1,000 mL.
- Estimated blood loss 350 mL (suction and sponges).
- Urine output 150 mL via Foley. No blood products given intraoperatively.

**Medications**
Phenylephrine 300 mcg total, propofol infusion, ondansetron 4 mg IV at closure. No intrathecal opioid used given age and risk of delirium and retention.

**Events / Complications**
None. No airway intervention.

**Postoperative Plan**
- PACU monitoring until spinal wears off and hemodynamics recover; expect motor return in 2-3 hours.
- Postoperative Hgb, treat hypotension with fluids first; consider transfusion if Hgb is below 8 or hypotension persists.
- Oxygen to keep SpO2 92% or higher; incentive spirometry once awake.
- Multimodal analgesia with scheduled acetaminophen; oxycodone PRN, lowest effective dose.
- Delirium precautions; report given to PACU nurse.

title: Operative Note - ORIF Right Intertrochanteric Fracture
author: A. Reyes, MD
summary: ORIF of the right intertrochanteric femur fracture with a cephalomedullary nail under spinal anesthesia, EBL 350 mL, no complications.
body:
**Procedure Note**
Date of surgery: 11/08/2026. Surgery 1430-1615.

**Preoperative Diagnosis**
Right intertrochanteric femur fracture.

**Postoperative Diagnosis**
Same (AO/OTA 31A2, comminuted, osteopenic bone).

**Procedure**
Closed reduction and internal fixation of the right intertrochanteric femur fracture with a short cephalomedullary (intramedullary) nail.

**Surgeon / Anesthesia**
Surgeon A. Reyes, MD. Anesthesia: spinal (K. Lindqvist, MD).

**Indications**
82-year-old woman with a displaced right intertrochanteric fracture after a fall. Risks, benefits and alternatives were reviewed with the patient and her daughter, who consented.

**Description**
Cefazolin 2 g IV was given at 1400. After spinal anesthesia she was positioned supine on the fracture table with the right leg in traction and the left leg supported. Fluoroscopy confirmed an acceptable closed reduction in AP and lateral views. The right hip and thigh were prepped and draped sterilely. A lateral proximal incision of about 5 cm was made, the entry point was identified and the canal reamed. A 10 mm x 180 mm 130-degree cephalomedullary nail was seated, and a 90 mm lag screw was placed in center-center position with a tip-apex distance of 18 mm. Set screw locked in dynamic mode. Final images showed good reduction and implant position. The wound was irrigated and closed in layers with 3 skin staples at the entry incision. Aquacel dressing applied.

**Findings**
Comminuted intertrochanteric fracture with posteromedial fragment and lesser trochanter involvement; poor-quality osteopenic bone. Good fixation at final fluoroscopy.

**Implants**
Short cephalomedullary nail 10 mm x 180 mm, 90 mm lag screw, set screw. No cement.

**EBL / Fluids / Urine**
Estimated blood loss 350 mL. See anesthesia record for fluids. Foley in place. No drains. No specimens. Sponge and instrument counts correct.

**Complications**
None.

**Condition / Disposition**
Stable, to PACU.

**Postoperative Plan**
- Weight bearing as tolerated on the right leg; PT/OT starting POD 1. No hip precautions.
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily starting the morning of POD 1 if hemostasis is acceptable, to complete 35 days of VTE prophylaxis total. SCD on the left leg.
- Cefazolin 2 g IV x2 more doses (2200 tonight and 0600) for a 24-hour course.
- Postoperative CBC in PACU and with morning labs; low threshold to transfuse given age and baseline Hgb 11.8.
- Neurovascular checks right leg q4h. Aquacel stays on until follow-up unless saturated.
- Multimodal pain control; no NSAIDs. Follow up with me in 2 weeks for staple removal and x-ray.

title: PACU Nursing Note
author: R. Vega, RN
summary: PACU course with hypotension and tachycardia after ORIF, Hgb 7.9, LR bolus given, oxygen weaned to 3 L, transfer to step-down pending.
body:
**Situation**
82-year-old woman, post-op day 0 after ORIF of the right intertrochanteric fracture (spinal anesthesia, EBL 350 mL), arrived in PACU at 1615. Hypotensive and tachycardic on arrival, anemic on the postoperative labs.

**Background**
HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a. Allergy: sulfa (rash). Lisinopril and metformin held. Foley in place (placed in the ED for retention).

**Assessment**
- 1630: T 97.6 F, HR 112, BP 86/48, RR 20, SpO2 92% on 4 L nasal cannula, pain 3/10.
- 1700: HR 108, BP 92/52, RR 20, SpO2 93% on 3 L, pain 3/10.
- 1745: T 97.9 F, HR 104, BP 98/56, RR 20, SpO2 94% on 3 L, pain 4/10.
- Labs 1630: Hgb 7.9 (11.4 this morning), Hct 23.7, WBC 11.0, platelets 190.
- Neuro: awake, oriented x4, mildly drowsy, follows commands; spinal block resolving with right foot movement returning.
- Resp: lungs clear, no distress; incentive spirometer teaching done.
- Right leg: Aquacel dressing dry and intact with no strike-through, thigh soft, foot warm, pulses palpable, sensation returning.
- GU: Foley draining clear yellow urine, adequate output.

**Interventions**
- Dr. Lindqvist and Dr. Patel notified of BP and Hgb. LR 500 mL bolus given for hypotension, with improving pressures (86/48 to 98/56). Oxygen weaned from 4 L to 3 L.
- Telemetry shows sinus tachycardia, no ectopy. Pain managed with acetaminophen, no opioid needed so far.
- Head of bed raised, heels floated, SCD on left leg. Daughter Karen Mills updated at the bedside.

**Recommendation / Handoff**
Accepted for step-down (Unit 4 West, SD-12) for post-op hypotension, anemia and oxygen need; transport expected about 1800 with telemetry. Report to be given nurse to nurse. Recheck BP and HR q15 minutes until transfer. Dr. Patel to evaluate the Hgb of 7.9 for transfusion; type and screen on file (A positive). Keep NPO until swallow and alertness reassessed, then advance as tolerated.

title: Hospitalist Note - Step-Down Transfer
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: Transferred to step-down for post-op hypotension, acute blood loss anemia (Hgb 7.9) and new oxygen need; transfusion 1 unit PRBC planned.
body:
**Reason for Transfer**
Seen on arrival to Step-Down Unit 4 West (SD-12) at 1820, POD 0 after ORIF of the right intertrochanteric fracture. Moved from PACU to a telemetry bed because of post-op hypotension, acute blood loss anemia, a new oxygen requirement, and age 82 with HTN, T2DM and CKD 3a.

**Interval History**
EBL 350 mL. In PACU BP nadir 86/48 with HR 112; improved to 98/56 after a 500 mL LR bolus. Hgb 7.9 (11.4 at 0600). She is comfortable, pain 5/10, no chest pain, dyspnea or lightheadedness.

**Objective**
- 1830: T 97.8 F, HR 102, BP 100/58, RR 20, SpO2 93% on 2 L nasal cannula.
- Awake, oriented x4. Lungs clear without crackles. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft.
- Right thigh: Aquacel dry, thigh soft, foot warm with palpable pulses. Foley draining clear yellow urine.
- Labs 1630: WBC 11.0, Hgb 7.9, Hct 23.7, platelets 190. Creatinine 1.1 this morning. Type and screen A positive.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. Acute blood loss anemia (surgical loss plus hemodilution), Hgb 7.9 with tachycardia and borderline pressures. Transfuse 1 unit PRBC, start 1930 over 3.5 hours, with vitals per protocol; watch for volume overload (mild cardiomegaly on chest x-ray). Post-transfusion CBC. Consent from patient and Karen.
2. Post-op hypotension, likely spinal vasodilation plus blood loss. Avoid further large boluses; recheck vitals q1h during transfusion. Telemetry continuous.
3. Oxygen: 2 L nasal cannula to keep SpO2 92% or higher, incentive spirometry hourly while awake, wean as tolerated.
4. Hypertension: hold lisinopril. Diabetes: hold metformin (CKD, acute illness); insulin lispro correction scale AC and HS. CKD 3a: avoid nephrotoxins, BMP and CBC in the morning.
5. VTE: SCD on the left leg; enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily to start Monday morning if Hgb is stable, per Dr. Reyes.
6. Antibiotics: cefazolin 2 g IV at 2200 and 0600 to complete 24 hours. Pain: acetaminophen scheduled, oxycodone PRN. Bowel regimen.
7. Foley in place from the ED for retention; strict I&O; will review need on POD 1.
8. Full Code. Daughter Karen updated by phone.

title: Orthopedic Progress Note - POD 1
author: A. Reyes, MD
summary: POD 1 after cephalomedullary nail: stable, incision clean, neurovascularly intact, WBAT, enoxaparin to start this morning.
body:
**Subjective**
Post-op day 1 after ORIF of the right intertrochanteric fracture with a cephalomedullary nail. Pain 4/10 at rest, controlled with scheduled acetaminophen and PRN oxycodone. No numbness or tingling in the right leg, no calf pain, no chest pain or dyspnea. Slept in short intervals. Transfused 1 unit PRBC overnight and tolerated it.

**Objective**
- 0700 vitals: T 98.4 F, HR 88, BP 116/66, RR 18, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula, pain 4/10.
- Alert and oriented x4, pleasant, follows commands.
- Right lateral thigh incision: Aquacel dressing dry and intact, no strike-through, no surrounding erythema or swelling. Dressing first checked today; no change needed. 3 staples at the entry site, not examined under the dressing.
- Thigh and calf soft, compartments compressible. Right foot warm, DP and PT pulses palpable, capillary refill under 2 s, sensation intact in all dermatomes, dorsiflexion and plantarflexion and toe movement intact.
- Labs 0530: WBC 10.2, Hgb 9.2 (7.9 pre-transfusion, 9.4 afterward), platelets 182, creatinine 1.3, K 4.2.
- Foley draining clear yellow urine.

**Assessment**
82-year-old woman POD 1 s/p right intertrochanteric fracture fixation with a cephalomedullary nail. Recovering as expected; hemoglobin stable after transfusion.

**Plan**
1. Weight bearing as tolerated on the right leg. PT and OT today, bed to chair. No hip precautions with an intramedullary nail.
2. Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily to start this morning (Hgb stable, no bleeding), continue for 35 days total. SCD on the left leg in bed.
3. Cefazolin course completes with the 0600 dose.
4. Keep Aquacel dressing on until follow-up unless saturated. Neurovascular checks q4h. Call for drainage over 3 cm, loss of pulse or new numbness.
5. Pain: continue acetaminophen 1,000 mg q8h and low-dose oxycodone PRN; bowel regimen.
6. Osteoporosis: fragility fracture. Continue calcium and vitamin D; alendronate to restart when she can sit upright 30 minutes; outpatient bone health follow-up.
7. Disposition: anticipate skilled nursing facility rehab given age, living alone and stairs at home; case management consulted. Medicine co-managing (Dr. Patel).

title: Hospitalist Progress Note - POD 1
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: POD 1: hemoglobin 9.2 after transfusion, BP recovered, lisinopril held, Foley kept for strict I&O with plan to remove soon, creatinine 1.3.
body:
**Interval History**
POD 1 after hip fracture fixation. Received 1 unit PRBC 1930-2300 with Hgb 9.4 afterward. Overnight no events; no chest pain, dyspnea or lightheadedness. Pain 4/10. Tolerating a consistent-carbohydrate diet. Not yet out of bed.

**Objective**
- 0700: T 98.4 F, HR 88, BP 116/66, RR 18, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula (room air trials this morning were not tolerated, desaturating to 90-91%).
- Recent trend: HR 112 to 88, SBP 86 to 116 since PACU. Telemetry sinus rhythm, no arrhythmia.
- Intake and output 0300-0700: in 520 mL, out 320 mL via Foley, clear yellow. Glucose 156 at 0730.
- Alert and oriented x4. Lungs clear with decreased bases. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Right thigh dressing dry; foot warm, pulses palpable. Legs without calf tenderness.
- Labs 0530: WBC 10.2, Hgb 9.2, platelets 182, Na 136, K 4.2, CO2 24, BUN 24, creatinine 1.3 (1.1 yesterday morning, baseline 1.2), eGFR 40, calcium 8.3, magnesium 1.8, glucose 160.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. Acute blood loss anemia, stable at 9.2 after 1 unit PRBC. No further transfusion; CBC in the morning.
2. Post-op hypotension, resolved. Continue to hold lisinopril today; reassess after tomorrow's creatinine.
3. Mild creatinine rise to 1.3 (CKD 3a, perioperative hypovolemia, blood loss). Continue maintenance LR 75 mL/h and encourage oral fluids; avoid NSAIDs and contrast; BMP daily. Hold metformin for now; correction-scale insulin AC and HS.
4. Hypoxemia, mild, postoperative atelectasis likely, with mild cardiomegaly on imaging but no signs of volume overload. Incentive spirometry every hour while awake, out of bed with PT, retry room air later today.
5. VTE: enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily starting today (CrCl about 32, acceptable) plus SCD on the left leg.
6. Foley: placed 11/07 in the ED for retention. It is being kept for strict I&O while she is on IV fluids and hemodynamics settle; I plan to remove it soon once she is mobilizing and drinking well. Daily necessity review.
7. T2DM: glucose 150-170s on correction scale. Hypothyroidism: continue levothyroxine. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin.
8. Rehabilitation: PT and OT today; case management evaluating for SNF.
9. Full Code. Karen Mills updated at the bedside.

title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
author: S. Kim, PT
summary: First PT session: moderate assist bed mobility and a bed-to-chair transfer with a walker, SNF rehab recommended.
body:
**Reason for Referral**
POD 1 after ORIF of the right intertrochanteric femur fracture with a cephalomedullary nail. Weight bearing as tolerated on the right leg; no hip precautions.

**Prior Level of Function**
Independent with a cane, drives, lives alone in a two-story house with the bedroom upstairs. Daughter Karen Mills lives 20 minutes away. Wears glasses and a left hearing aid.

**Subjective**
Reports right hip pain 5/10 with movement, 4/10 at rest. "I just want to get home." Motivated and cooperative. Alert and oriented x4, follows commands, hearing aid on.

**Objective**
- Vitals at rest: HR 88-90, SpO2 94-95% on 2 L nasal cannula, BP 118/68; SpO2 stayed at 93-94% with activity. No dizziness on sitting.
- Foley and IV in place. Aquacel dressing dry. Right foot warm, sensation intact, toe movement intact.
- Bed mobility: moderate assist x1 for the right leg and trunk. Supine to sit with a slow sit and no dizziness.
- Sit to stand: moderate assist x1 with a rolling walker, cues for weight shift to the left and for hand placement. Stood about 1 minute with fair standing balance.
- Transfer bed to chair with a stand-pivot: moderate assist x1, tolerated well. Did not ambulate yet. Right hip flexion and abduction limited by pain; left leg strength 4/5.
- Fall risk: high (Morse high).

**Assessment**
Impaired mobility, balance and strength after hip fracture fixation. Pain limits right weight bearing but she is able to bear weight as tolerated. Good rehabilitation potential given motivation and prior independence. Home is not safe at present: lives alone with a bedroom upstairs.

**Plan / Recommendations**
- PT daily: transfers, gait training with a rolling walker, strengthening, stairs when ready.
- Premedicate before therapy; ice to the thigh as needed.
- Out of bed to chair for meals, with 1 assist and walker, bed alarm on.
- Discharge recommendation: skilled nursing facility for short-term rehabilitation, then home with home health PT.
- Goals in 7-10 days: transfers with stand-by assist, ambulate 150 ft with walker, up and down 4 steps with rail.

title: Occupational Therapy Initial Evaluation
author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
summary: OT evaluation: needs moderate to maximal assist for lower body ADLs after hip fixation, SNF rehab recommended.
body:
**Reason for Referral**
POD 1 s/p right intertrochanteric femur fracture fixation. Weight bearing as tolerated, no hip precautions.

**Prior Level of Function**
Independent in basic and instrumental ADLs, drives, manages her own medications and pill box, cooks, uses a cane. Lives alone in a two-story house with a tub shower on the second floor.

**Subjective**
"I need to be able to take care of myself." Pain 4/10 at rest, 5/10 with movement. Cooperative and motivated.

**Objective**
- Cognition: alert and oriented x4, follows 3-step commands, intact short-term memory on screening. Wears glasses; left hearing aid in place.
- Vitals: HR 90, SpO2 94% on 2 L nasal cannula, BP 118/68 at rest.
- Upper extremity strength and range of motion within functional limits bilaterally.
- Grooming: set-up and supervision seated at the bedside.
- Upper body dressing: supervision. Lower body dressing: maximal assist for the right leg and pants over the feet. Bathing: moderate assist.
- Toileting: Foley in place; toilet transfer not yet attempted. Sit to stand with walker: moderate assist x1.
- Balance: sitting good, standing fair with walker.

**Assessment**
Decline in self-care from independent to moderate and maximal assist due to pain, weakness and mobility limits after hip fixation. Good rehabilitation potential. Home environment with a second-floor bedroom and bathroom is a barrier.

**Plan / Recommendations**
- OT daily for ADL retraining, lower-body dressing technique, energy conservation, toilet and shower transfers, and home safety.
- Adaptive equipment: reacher, sock aid, long-handled sponge and shoehorn; raised toilet seat and shower chair for rehab and home.
- Discharge recommendation: skilled nursing facility with continued OT, then home with home health and a home safety evaluation.
- Educated patient on weight bearing as tolerated and positioning; she verbalized understanding.

title: Dietitian Nutrition Assessment
author: P. Moreno, RD
summary: Nutrition assessment: low risk, adequate weight and BMI, protein supplement twice daily to support wound and fracture healing.
body:
**Reason for Consult**
Hip fracture with surgery, POD 1, type 2 diabetes. Nutrition screening: moderate risk because of surgery and reduced intake.

**Anthropometrics**
Height 160 cm, weight 61 kg, BMI 23.8. Usual body weight about 62 kg per patient, no recent unintentional loss.

**Pertinent Data**
- Diet order: consistent-carbohydrate, 2 g sodium. Eating about 50% of meals since surgery; no nausea or vomiting. Bowel movement not yet recorded this admission.
- Labs: A1c 7.2%, glucose 142-172, creatinine 1.3 (eGFR 40), BUN 24, K 4.2, calcium 8.3, magnesium 1.8, 25-OH vitamin D 22 ng/mL (low), Hgb 9.2.
- Medications: calcium with vitamin D, senna-docusate, polyethylene glycol, levothyroxine, insulin correction scale.
- Skin: surgical incision right lateral thigh, no pressure injury.

**Estimated Needs**
- Energy: 25-30 kcal/kg, about 1,525-1,830 kcal/day.
- Protein: 1.2-1.5 g/kg, about 73-92 g/day for healing and fracture recovery; CKD 3a does not require restriction at this stage.
- Fluid: at least 1,500 mL/day unless told otherwise.

**Assessment**
At nutrition risk from surgery and reduced intake but no malnutrition criteria at this time. Intake is expected to improve as pain and mobility improve. Low vitamin D and fragility fracture support continued calcium and vitamin D.

**Plan / Interventions**
1. Continue consistent-carbohydrate, 2 g sodium diet.
2. Diabetic-appropriate oral nutrition supplement twice daily (between meals) for added protein, about 220 kcal and 16 g protein each.
3. Encourage fluids and high-fiber foods; bowel regimen per orders.
4. Meal set-up and help opening containers; glasses and hearing aid on at meals.
5. Recommend recheck of vitamin D status and bone health plan after discharge (SNF physician or PCP).
6. Dietitian will follow; goal meal intake 75% or more within 3 days.

title: Case Management Initial Assessment
author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
summary: Initial discharge assessment: lives alone in a two-story house, daughter Karen involved, SNF rehab recommended and referrals sent.
body:
**Reason for Assessment**
82-year-old woman admitted 11/08 with a right hip fracture, POD 1 after ORIF. Discharge planning evaluation.

**Home Situation**
- Widow, lives alone in a two-story house; bedroom and full bathroom are upstairs, with a half bath on the main floor.
- Independent in ADLs before admission, drives, uses a cane. No home health or services before this admission.
- Daughter Karen Mills (health care proxy) lives 20 minutes away and visits daily. She is willing to help but works full time and cannot provide 24-hour assistance.
- Insurance: Medicare Part A and B. Qualifying inpatient stay meets the 3-midnight rule by Wednesday.

**Clinical Status / Therapy Recommendations**
Per PT (S. Kim): moderate assist for transfers, bed to chair today, not yet ambulatory. Per OT (H. Larsen): moderate to maximal assist for lower body ADLs. Both recommend short-term SNF rehabilitation. Medically: on oxygen 2 L, Foley in place, enoxaparin started, anticipate readiness for transfer about POD 3-4.

**Patient and Family Preferences**
Patient's goal is to return home after rehab. She and Karen understand that she cannot safely manage stairs or live alone right now and agree to SNF rehabilitation. Provided the Medicare list of skilled nursing facilities with quality ratings and the right to choose. Preference is a facility close to Karen's home with daily therapy.

**Plan**
1. Referrals sent today through the electronic system to three facilities, including Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation. Awaiting bed offers.
2. Will confirm clinical readiness, prepare transfer summary and arrange transport once a bed is accepted.
3. Medicare patient rights notice reviewed and signed.
4. Equipment needs: rolling walker will be provided by the SNF; discuss home equipment before eventual discharge home.
5. Will follow daily; update team on bed offers and anticipated transfer date.

title: Pharmacy Medication Reconciliation
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: Admission medication reconciliation: home medications verified, holds and renal dosing reviewed.
body:
**Sources**
Patient interview with daughter Karen Mills present, pharmacy fill history and pill box description. Allergy: sulfa antibiotics (rash), verified.

**Home Medications (verified)**
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily. Inpatient: held since 11/08 for post-op hypotension; resume when SBP is consistently above 110 and creatinine stable.
- Metformin 500 mg PO BID. Inpatient: held (acute illness, creatinine 1.3, eGFR 40). Insulin lispro correction scale in use instead.
- Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily at 0600. Continued. TSH 2.1 on 11/08.
- Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly. Continued.
- Alendronate 70 mg PO weekly (Sundays). Held; patient cannot remain upright 30 minutes. Restart when able to sit up for 30 minutes after dosing.
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg with vitamin D 400 units PO BID. Continued.
- No OTC NSAIDs, supplements or herbals reported. Adherence reported good with a weekly pill box.

**Inpatient Medications Reviewed**
Acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO q8h (max 3 g/day); oxycodone 2.5-5 mg PO q4h PRN; enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily; senna-docusate, polyethylene glycol, bisacodyl PR PRN; ondansetron PRN; lactated Ringer's 75 mL/h; cefazolin 24-hour course completed 0600.

**Pharmacy Assessment**
1. Renal function: creatinine 1.3, estimated CrCl about 32 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault, 61 kg). Enoxaparin 40 mg daily is appropriate (CrCl above 30). Avoid NSAIDs.
2. Beers considerations: oxycodone and any sedatives raise delirium and fall risk; use the lowest dose, no benzodiazepines, no diphenhydramine.
3. Vitamin D 22 ng/mL (low): recommend adding vitamin D3 1,000 units daily to the calcium with D at transfer (for provider consideration).
4. No drug interactions of concern. No duplicate acetaminophen products; total acetaminophen not to exceed 3 g in 24 hours.
5. Bowel regimen appropriate for opioid use.

**Plan**
Reconciliation entered. Will reassess for resumption of lisinopril and metformin with provider and complete a transfer reconciliation at discharge.

title: Hospitalist Progress Note - POD 2
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: POD 2: stable, Hgb 9.0, creatinine 1.3, BP stable, oxygen wean planned, lisinopril held until tomorrow, SNF disposition.
body:
**Interval History**
POD 2 after right hip ORIF. No overnight events. Pain 4/10 on acetaminophen and PRN oxycodone. Sat at the bedside and in the chair yesterday with PT. Appetite fair. Bowel movement yesterday. No chest pain, dyspnea or palpitations.

**Objective**
- 0700: T 98.6 F, HR 88, BP 118/66, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula, pain 4/10.
- Stable BP 116-124/66-70 over the last 24 hours. Telemetry: sinus rhythm, no events.
- Alert and oriented x4. Lungs clear, slightly diminished at the bases. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, bowel sounds present. No calf tenderness.
- Right thigh Aquacel dressing dry and intact; foot warm, pulses palpable.
- Foley draining clear yellow urine, about 60 mL/h (0300-0700: out 260 mL). LR 75 mL/h running.
- Labs 0500: WBC 11.2 (10.2 yesterday), Hgb 9.0, platelets 176, Na 137, K 4.1, CO2 25, BUN 26, creatinine 1.3, eGFR 40, calcium 8.4, magnesium 1.9, glucose 154.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. Acute blood loss anemia, stable Hgb 9.0. No transfusion; CBC daily. Continue enoxaparin 40 mg daily (day 2).
2. Mild leukocytosis 11.2, likely postoperative stress response; afebrile, lungs clear, incision clean. Recheck with CBC in the morning.
3. Post-op hypoxemia: still on 2 L. Stop LR at 0900 as she is drinking well. Wean oxygen to room air today as tolerated with a goal SpO2 94% or higher at rest and with therapy; hourly incentive spirometry and out of bed.
4. CKD 3a with creatinine 1.3, stable. Lisinopril remains held; plan to resume after tomorrow morning's creatinine if it is stable and SBP stays above 110. Metformin held; correction-scale insulin with glucose 140-180.
5. Foley day 4 remains in place for strict I&O; reassess need today.
6. Pain: continue scheduled acetaminophen, oxycodone PRN with PT premedication; bowel regimen.
7. Disposition: PT and OT recommend SNF; case management has referrals out. Anticipate transfer Wednesday if oxygen weaned and stable.
8. Full Code. Daughter Karen visits this morning; plan reviewed.

title: Orthopedic Progress Note - POD 2
author: A. Reyes, MD
summary: POD 2 ortho: incision clean, neurovascularly intact, WBAT with PT, staples out at 2-week follow-up.
body:
**Subjective**
POD 2 after cephalomedullary nail for a right intertrochanteric fracture. Pain 4/10 at rest, higher with therapy. No numbness, tingling or calf pain. Out of bed to the chair with PT yesterday. Denies fever or chills.

**Objective**
- 0700 vitals: T 98.6 F, HR 88, BP 118/66, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula.
- Incision, right lateral thigh: Aquacel dressing dry and intact with no drainage; edges and skin around the dressing without erythema, warmth or swelling. Three staples at the entry site lie beneath the dressing and were not disturbed.
- Thigh swollen mildly as expected, compartments soft. Mild bruising along the lateral thigh.
- Neurovascular: right foot warm, DP and PT pulses palpable, capillary refill under 2 s, sensation intact, dorsiflexion, plantarflexion and toe movement intact. No calf tenderness.
- Hgb 9.0 stable. Creatinine 1.3.

**Assessment**
POD 2, recovering well after fixation with a cephalomedullary nail. Pain controlled. No signs of wound complication or compartment syndrome.

**Plan**
1. Weight bearing as tolerated right leg; PT and OT daily. No hip precautions.
2. Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily for 35 days total; left leg SCD in bed.
3. Leave Aquacel in place until the follow-up visit unless saturated or soiled. Call for drainage over 3 cm or fever.
4. Staple removal and repeat x-ray at follow-up with me in 2 weeks.
5. Continue pain regimen; encourage incentive spirometry.
6. Osteoporosis: restart alendronate when able to sit upright 30 minutes (can be done at the SNF); continue calcium and vitamin D; bone health referral after discharge.
7. Agree with SNF rehab. Ortho will sign off to outpatient follow-up at transfer.

title: Physical Therapy Treatment Note
author: S. Kim, PT
summary: POD 2 PT: stood with a walker and 1 assist and walked 10 ft, pain 6/10 with activity after oxycodone.
body:
**Subjective**
POD 2 treatment session. Oxycodone 5 mg given at 0830 before therapy. Pain 6/10 with activity, 4/10 at rest. "It's sore but I want to try."

**Objective**
- Vitals at rest: HR 86, BP 120/68, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula. With activity HR rose to 94 and SpO2 held at 93-94%, recovering within 2 minutes of sitting.
- Lines: Foley, peripheral IV with LR running (stopped at 0900), nasal cannula. Aquacel dressing dry.
- Bed mobility: moderate assist to minimal assist x1 for the right leg.
- Sat at the edge of the bed 3 minutes with good balance, no dizziness.
- Sit to stand with rolling walker and 1 person assist: completed twice, stood 2 minutes.
- Gait: walked 10 ft with the walker and 1 assist, with a slow step-to gait, good weight shift to the right as tolerated, short rest after 10 ft due to pain and fatigue.
- Transfer to chair with 1 assist; remained up in the chair after the session with call light and bed alarm.
- Alert, oriented x4, follows commands. Hearing aid and glasses on.

**Assessment**
Improved from yesterday's transfer-only status to walking 10 ft. Activity tolerance and pain with weight bearing remain the main limits. High fall risk. Tolerates weight bearing as tolerated.

**Plan**
- Continue PT daily; advance gait distance and sit-to-stand repetitions.
- Premedicate 30 minutes before sessions. Ice after therapy.
- Up to chair for meals with 1 assist and walker; bed alarm on.
- Continue to recommend SNF rehabilitation. Educated on use of the walker and incentive spirometer; patient verbalized understanding.

title: Occupational Therapy Treatment Note
author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
summary: POD 2 OT: seated grooming and dressing training, stood with walker and 1 assist, adaptive equipment trained.
body:
**Subjective**
POD 2 treatment. Pain 6/10 with activity after oxycodone 5 mg at 0830, 4/10 at rest. Feels tired but wants to do more for herself.

**Objective**
- Vitals: HR 86, BP 120/68, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula at rest. SpO2 93-94% during activity.
- Grooming: seated at the edge of the bed, set-up only; washed face and brushed teeth independently.
- Upper body dressing: independent seated. Lower body dressing with reacher and sock aid: moderate assist for the right leg, improved from maximal assist.
- Stood with rolling walker and 1 assist at the bedside for about 2 minutes while hygiene was completed. Transfer bed to chair with 1 assist, about 10 ft.
- Foley in place, so toilet transfer not attempted. Bathing at sink deferred.
- Cognition: alert and oriented x4, follows 2-step commands, good carryover of adaptive equipment instructions. Glasses and left hearing aid on.

**Assessment**
Making steady progress with seated ADLs and standing tolerance. Still needs moderate assist for lower body dressing and 1 assist for standing tasks. Fatigue and pain limit endurance. Good potential for functional recovery.

**Plan**
- Continue OT daily; progress to standing grooming, toilet transfer with raised seat once catheter is out, and lower body dressing with equipment.
- Educate on energy conservation and pacing activity with rest breaks.
- Recommend SNF rehab, then home with home safety evaluation, raised toilet seat and shower chair.
- Patient left up in the chair with call light in reach, bed alarm on and Karen expected later this morning.

title: Case Management Note
author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
summary: Maple Grove accepted at 1400, transfer to SNF expected Wednesday.
body:
**Update**
Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation accepted the referral at 1400 today and has a bed for Wednesday. The admitting nurse is C. Pruitt, RN.

**Discussion with Patient and Family**
Reviewed the acceptance with the patient and her daughter Karen Mills, who was at the bedside this afternoon. Both agreed to Maple Grove, which is about 15 minutes from Karen's home. Patient understands that this is short-term rehabilitation with the goal of returning to her own home. Karen has no concerns and will bring the patient's glasses, left hearing aid, cane, clothes and shoes on Wednesday.

**Clinical Readiness**
- Per Dr. Patel, transfer is expected Wednesday morning or early afternoon if she remains stable.
- Weaned to room air at 1400 today with SpO2 94%; no oxygen needs for the facility.
- PT: walked 10 ft with walker and 1 assist this morning. OT: standing tolerance improving. Both recommend daily therapy at the SNF.
- Medicare Part A skilled benefit; qualifying 3-midnight inpatient stay will be met. No prior authorization required.

**Plan**
1. Final transfer time and transport to be set after Dr. Patel clears the patient Wednesday morning. Wheelchair van will be arranged.
2. Prepare transfer summary, medication reconciliation and orders for the SNF with Dr. Patel and Pharmacy.
3. Nurse-to-nurse report to C. Pruitt before departure.
4. Will update the nurse and Karen with the exact time tomorrow.

title: Night Hospitalist Event Note - Fever and New Confusion
author: N. Ahmed, MD
summary: Called 2115 for T 100.8 F and new confusion; assessed as catheter-associated UTI, cultures sent, Foley removed, ceftriaxone chosen.
body:
**Reason for Evaluation**
Called by the night nurse (P. Dalton, RN) at 2115 about a temperature of 100.8 F at 2100 and new confusion in a POD 2 patient. Seen at the bedside.

**History**
82-year-old woman POD 2 after right hip ORIF. Foley placed in the ED on 11/07 at 2330 for retention and left in for strict I&O (catheter day 5). Per day nursing, the urine looked cloudy with a stronger odor at 1500 care, temperature crept up from 99.3 F at 1500 to 99.8 F at 1900 and 100.1 F at 2000, and she was transiently confused at dinner (asked about her husband) and restless this evening, picking at the catheter and saying "I need to go". Baseline is alert and oriented, no dementia. She reports mild lower abdominal discomfort. No cough, dyspnea, flank pain, vomiting, diarrhea, calf pain or incisional pain change.

**Objective**
- 2100: T 100.8 F, HR 102, BP 112/62, RR 20, SpO2 93% on room air, pain 5/10. 2130: T 100.9 F, HR 104, BP 112/60. 2200: T 100.9 F, HR 106, BP 110/60, RR 21, SpO2 93%. Glucose 188 at 2100.
- Appears tired, restless, oriented to person only, inattentive, CAM positive. Follows commands, no focal deficit. Mucous membranes slightly dry.
- Lungs clear bilaterally, no crackles, no increased work of breathing. Heart tachycardic, regular.
- Abdomen soft with suprapubic tenderness, no guarding. No CVA tenderness bilaterally. Foley draining cloudy dark yellow urine.
- Right thigh incision: Aquacel dry and intact, no erythema or drainage. Calves soft and nontender, no swelling. Right foot warm with pulses.
- Labs drawn at 2145 (CBC, BMP, lactate) and UA with culture; blood cultures x2 at 2150. Results pending. Last labs: WBC 11.2, creatinine 1.3 (0500).

**Assessment**
New fever and acute delirium in an older woman with a catheter in place for almost 5 days: most consistent with catheter-associated UTI. Other causes were considered: pneumonia (lungs clear, no cough, room air sats stable), surgical site infection (incision clean), DVT or PE (no calf signs, no chest pain, SpO2 93%), and medication-related delirium (oxycodone 2.5-5 mg PRN over the last day; contributes but does not explain fever). Hemodynamically stable. No hypotension; lactate pending.

**Plan / Orders**
1. UA with culture from the catheter sampling port (not the bag) collected before antibiotics. Blood cultures x2, CBC, BMP, lactate. Urinalysis result pending (expected about 2230).
2. Foley removed at 2200 after the specimen was collected (no remaining indication). Bladder scan after removal; call if residual over 300 mL or no void in 6 hours. Strict I&O, toileting q2h.
3. Push oral fluids. Scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg given at 2200 as scheduled; do not stack the PRN 650 mg dose.
4. Antibiotic: ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h, first dose after cultures, ordered. Reasoning: sulfa allergy rules out TMP-SMX; fluoroquinolones avoided because of age 82, active delirium, QT and tendon risk; ceftriaxone needs no renal adjustment at CrCl about 32 mL/min; she tolerated cefazolin this admission. Will narrow to the culture.
5. Delirium precautions: glasses and left hearing aid on, reorient, lights on and quiet at night, bed alarm, no new sedatives or anticholinergics, limit oxycodone, avoid restraints.
6. Vitals q2h; call for SBP under 100, HR over 120, T over 101.5 F, new lethargy, or SpO2 under 92%. Telemetry continues.
7. Will recheck results and notify the family: Karen Mills (proxy) to be updated by phone.

title: Night Hospitalist Result Note
author: N. Ahmed, MD
summary: UA consistent with infection, WBC 14.6, lactate 1.5, ceftriaxone ordered for 2330; not septic.
body:
**Results Review**
Follow-up to my 2220 note on fever and new confusion with a catheter-associated UTI suspected.

- UA 2230: cloudy dark yellow, specific gravity 1.018, leukocyte esterase large, nitrite positive, WBC greater than 50/hpf, bacteria many, RBC 5-10/hpf, blood small. Positive for infection.
- CBC (2145): WBC 14.6 (11.2 this morning, 8.4 on admission), Hgb 9.0, platelets 172.
- BMP: Na 137, K 4.0, CO2 24, BUN 27, creatinine 1.3 (baseline), glucose 188.
- Lactate 1.5 mmol/L (normal).
- Urine culture and blood cultures x2: collected before antibiotics, in process.

**Clinical Update**
Foley removed at 2200 after the sampling-port specimen. 2230: T 100.6 F, HR 102, BP 112/62, SpO2 94% on room air. 2300: T 100.4 F, HR 100, BP 114/62, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air. She is calmer, still intermittently confused, tolerating sips. Scheduled acetaminophen given at 2200.

**Assessment**
Catheter-associated UTI with fever, leukocytosis and acute delirium. She meets SIRS criteria (temperature, heart rate, WBC) but I do not consider this sepsis: BP stable (MAP about 79), lactate normal, creatinine at baseline, platelets normal and no hypoxemia. Delirium is attributed to the febrile UTI in an older adult. Pneumonia, surgical site infection and DVT/PE remain unlikely on exam.

**Plan**
1. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h ordered and to be given at 2330 (cultures obtained first). Monitor for rash or reaction; sulfa allergy does not cross-react.
2. Follow urine and blood cultures; adjust the antibiotic to susceptibilities.
3. Continue oral fluids; if SBP falls below 100 or lactate rises, give 500 mL LR and repeat lactate. Repeat CBC in the morning.
4. Bladder scan after removal and strict I&O; she should void within 6 hours of removal.
5. Delirium precautions and fall precautions with bed alarm. Hold PRN oxycodone unless pain is 7/10 or higher.
6. Vitals q2h overnight. Notify me for any decline, and the day team (Dr. Patel) to review in the morning. Karen Mills to be updated.

title: Hospitalist Progress Note - POD 3
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: POD 3: improving after treatment for CAUTI, afebrile, confusion resolved, voiding, plan SNF transfer today.
body:
**Overnight Events**
Fever and new confusion Tuesday night, evaluated by Dr. Ahmed and treated as a catheter-associated UTI. Cultures sent, Foley removed at 2200, and ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 2330. Tmax 100.9 F at 2130-2200. She improved overnight: T 100.2 at 0000, 99.4 at 0300, 98.9 at 0600, and she has been afebrile since 0600. Confusion cleared by 0500 and CAM was negative at 0600. First void 0215 (220 mL) with a post-void scan of 80 mL; voiding spontaneously since.

**Subjective**
Feels better, no suprapubic pain, no dysuria, no flank pain. Pain 3/10. Eating breakfast. Oriented and talkative.

**Objective**
- 0700: T 98.8 F, HR 82, BP 128/70, RR 17, SpO2 96% on room air.
- Intake and output 0300-0700: in 380 mL, out 260 mL voided.
- Alert and oriented x4, CAM negative. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no suprapubic tenderness. No CVA tenderness. Incision dressing dry, foot warm.
- Labs 0500: WBC 12.1 (14.6), Hgb 9.3, platelets 181, Na 138, K 4.1, BUN 25, creatinine 1.2 (eGFR 44), calcium 8.5, glucose 163.
- Micro: urine culture pending. Blood cultures x2 pending, preliminary read due at 0800.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. Catheter-associated UTI, improving; clinically responding to ceftriaxone, afebrile, WBC down to 12.1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g IM daily for a total of 3 days (day 1 was 2330 Tuesday), then tailor the agent and duration to the final urine culture. No Foley; do not reinsert unless retention.
2. Delirium, resolved. Continue delirium precautions, glasses and hearing aid.
3. Hypertension/CKD: creatinine back to 1.2 and BP 128/70, so resume lisinopril 10 mg today at 0900 (SBP over 110). Metformin to resume at the SNF after the Friday BMP.
4. Acute blood loss anemia stable, Hgb 9.3. VTE: enoxaparin 40 mg daily for 35 days total.
5. Telemetry: no arrhythmia; discontinue telemetry now.
6. Diabetes: correction scale; glucose 150-210 during fever, now 163.
7. Disposition: transfer to Maple Grove SNF today. Stable for transfer if she continues to void and remains afebrile. PT/OT this morning. Transfer summary and medication reconciliation in progress. Karen Mills updated by phone.

title: Physical Therapy Treatment Note
author: S. Kim, PT
summary: POD 3 PT: walked 40 ft with a walker and stand-by assist, confusion resolved, SNF transfer today.
body:
**Subjective**
POD 3. Oxycodone 2.5 mg at 0830 before therapy. Pain 4/10 at rest, 5/10 with walking. "I feel much better than last night." Aware she is going to Maple Grove today. Mental status back to baseline after last night's confusion; alert and oriented x4.

**Objective**
- Vitals: HR 80, BP 134/74, RR 17, SpO2 96% on room air, T 98.7 F. Remained at SpO2 95-96% with walking, HR peak 92.
- No Foley. Peripheral IV in left forearm. Aquacel dressing dry.
- Bed mobility: stand-by assist with use of rail. Sit to stand with rolling walker: stand-by assist, good hand placement without cues.
- Gait: walked 40 ft with the walker and stand-by assist, improved from 10 ft yesterday, with a step-through pattern and good weight shift to the right as tolerated. One seated rest after 40 ft.
- Chair transfer: stand-by assist. Balance fair+ in standing with walker.
- Stairs not yet attempted.

**Assessment**
Strong progress today, now walking 40 ft with stand-by assist, weight bearing as tolerated. Fever and delirium episode did not set back mobility. Remains a high fall risk and needs daily skilled therapy to work toward stairs and home.

**Plan / Recommendations**
- Transfer to SNF for daily PT: gait progression to 150 ft, sit-to-stand strength, balance, and stair training with rail.
- Continue walker; weight bearing as tolerated right leg; no hip precautions.
- Fall precautions with a toileting schedule. Premedicate before therapy.
- Patient and Karen educated; walker was used for all transfers today. Handoff to receiving PT in the transfer paperwork.

title: Occupational Therapy Treatment Note
author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
summary: POD 3 OT: toilet transfer with raised seat and stand-by assist, improved lower body dressing, SNF OT recommended.
body:
**Subjective**
POD 3. Pain 3-4/10, premedicated with oxycodone 2.5 mg at 0830. Feels clear-headed this morning, no confusion. Voiding spontaneously since early this morning after the catheter was removed last night.

**Objective**
- Vitals: HR 80, BP 134/74, SpO2 96% on room air.
- Toilet transfer: walked to the bathroom with the walker and stand-by assist; used a raised toilet seat with stand-by assist for sit-to-stand and clothing management. Voided 180 mL, hygiene completed with supervision.
- Lower body dressing: minimal assist with reacher and sock aid (improved from moderate assist).
- Grooming standing at the sink with the walker: stand-by assist for 3 minutes.
- Cognition: alert and oriented x4, CAM negative, no confusion.
- Bathing: sponge bath seated, minimal assist.

**Assessment**
Making good functional gains. Needs stand-by to minimal assist for toileting and lower body ADLs. Continues to need skilled OT for lower body dressing, bathing and home preparation. Good potential to return to prior level.

**Plan / Recommendations**
- Continue OT daily at the SNF: bathing and toilet transfers, standing endurance, adaptive equipment, kitchen tasks.
- Equipment for eventual home: raised toilet seat, shower chair, reacher, sock aid; home safety evaluation before discharge from rehab.
- Reviewed toileting schedule and hydration. Karen to be present for caregiver training at the SNF.

title: Microbiology Result Note
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: Preliminary urine culture shows gram-negative rods over 100,000 CFU/mL, blood cultures no growth to date, ceftriaxone continues.
body:
**Results**
- Urine culture (catheter sampling port, collected 11/10 2145), preliminary at 0930: gram-negative rods, greater than 100,000 CFU/mL. Identification and susceptibilities to follow.
- Blood cultures x2 (peripheral, collected 11/10 2150), read at 0800: no growth to date (about 10 hours of incubation).

**Clinical Status**
Afebrile since 0600 (T 98.7 F at 0900), HR 80, BP 134/74, SpO2 96% on room air. Confusion resolved. Voiding spontaneously. WBC 12.1 this morning, down from 14.6. Creatinine 1.2.

**Assessment**
Culture-proven catheter-associated UTI with a gram-negative organism, consistent with the urinalysis, responding clinically to ceftriaxone. Blood cultures negative so far; these remain preliminary and will be finalized at 5 days.

**Plan**
1. Continue ceftriaxone 1 g daily (IM from today; dose 2 at 2330 tonight at the SNF, total 3 days initially), as gram-negative rods are expected to be susceptible. The final organism and susceptibilities will tailor the agent and the total duration.
2. The final urine culture will result on Thursday after transfer. Maple Grove will follow the final culture, and our team will also forward it. Ask the SNF physician to review the susceptibilities and change therapy if the organism is resistant to ceftriaxone.
3. Blood cultures continue to be monitored; will notify the facility if positive.
4. Return precautions: new fever, confusion, rigors, hypotension or flank pain.
5. No urinary catheter at transfer. Bladder scan for no void in 6 hours.

title: Pharmacy Transfer Medication Reconciliation
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: Transfer medication reconciliation for Maple Grove: continue list, resumed and held medications, sulfa allergy and TMP-SMX avoidance.
body:
**Reason**
Medication reconciliation for transfer to Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation today. Allergy: sulfa antibiotics (rash). Weight 61 kg, creatinine 1.2, eGFR 44, CrCl about 35 mL/min.

**Medications to Continue**
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily at 0900 for VTE prophylaxis, 35 days total from the first dose on 11/09 (last dose 12/13). Today's dose given 0900; next due Thursday 0900.
- Ceftriaxone 1 g IM once daily for catheter-associated UTI. Day 1 was IV on 11/10 at 2330; day 2 due tonight at 2330 at the SNF; day 3 Thursday at 2330, then adjust to the final culture and susceptibilities.
- Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily at 0600 (next Thursday 0600).
- Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly.
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg with vitamin D 400 units PO BID; vitamin D was low (22 ng/mL), consider adding vitamin D3 1,000 units daily.
- Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily, resumed today (0930 dose given; BP 134/74, creatinine 1.2). Hold for SBP under 110.
- Acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO q8h scheduled (0600, 1400, 2200); maximum 3 g per day from all sources.
- Oxycodone 2.5 mg PO q4h PRN pain 4-6, 5 mg PRN pain 7-10; last dose 0830. Lowest effective dose; delirium and fall risk. Controlled-substance prescription provided.
- Bowel regimen: senna-docusate 2 tablets BID and polyethylene glycol 17 g daily; bisacodyl 10 mg PR PRN.
- Glucose: check before meals and at bedtime with insulin lispro correction scale; metformin 500 mg BID to resume after the Friday BMP if creatinine is stable (eGFR above 30).

**Held / Changed**
- Alendronate 70 mg weekly: held in hospital; restart at the SNF when she can sit upright 30 minutes after taking it with a full glass of water.
- Metformin: held, plan above. Cefazolin and IV fluids: completed. Ondansetron: not needed.

**Safety Counseling**
1. Avoid TMP-SMX and other sulfonamide antibiotics (sulfa rash allergy).
2. Avoid fluoroquinolones if possible (age, delirium risk). No NSAIDs (CKD, enoxaparin).
3. Avoid benzodiazepines and diphenhydramine.
4. Patient and Karen Mills reviewed the list and given a printed copy; they had no questions. List sent with the transfer summary.

title: Discharge / Transfer Summary
author: S. Patel, MD
summary: Transfer summary to Maple Grove SNF after right hip ORIF, with catheter-associated UTI treated, pending cultures and follow-up plans.
body:
**Admission / Transfer**
Doris Kowalczyk, 82, DOB 1944-02-09, MRN SIM-40202. ED arrival 11/07 2215; admitted 11/08. Transferring 11/11 at 1430 to Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation. Attending Dr. S. Patel; surgeon Dr. A. Reyes. Allergy: sulfa antibiotics (rash). Code status: Full Code. Health care proxy: daughter Karen Mills.

**Diagnoses**
1. Right intertrochanteric femur fracture after a fall, s/p ORIF with cephalomedullary nail 11/08.
2. Acute blood loss anemia, transfused 1 unit PRBC.
3. Catheter-associated UTI (gram-negative rods) with fever and delirium, treated.
4. Chronic: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, hyperlipidemia.

**Hospital Course**
- Fall on 11/07; fixation on 11/08 under spinal anesthesia (EBL 350 mL). Post-op hypotension and Hgb 7.9 treated with fluids and 1 unit PRBC; Hgb 9.0-9.4 since, 9.3 today. Moved to step-down for monitoring and oxygen; weaned to room air 11/10 at 1400.
- Enoxaparin started 11/09. Weight bearing as tolerated; walked 40 ft with a walker and stand-by assist today.
- Foley placed in the ED 11/07 2330 for retention (UA then negative) and kept for strict I&O until 11/10 2200. On 11/10 she developed T 100.8-100.9 F, HR up to 106, suprapubic tenderness and delirium. UA positive, WBC 14.6, lactate 1.5, no sepsis. Cultures drawn, catheter removed, ceftriaxone started 11/10 2330. Afebrile since 0600, confusion resolved, WBC 12.1, voiding spontaneously (bladder scan 60 mL at 1100).
- Lisinopril held for hypotension and creatinine, resumed 11/11. Creatinine 1.2.

**Pending Results**
- Urine culture: preliminary gram-negative rods over 100,000 CFU/mL; identification and susceptibilities final Thursday 11/12.
- Blood cultures x2: no growth to date; final in 5 days.

**Condition at Transfer**
Vitals at 1100: T 98.6 F, HR 78, BP 132/72, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air, pain 3/10. Eating about 75%. Alert and oriented x4. Incision dressing dry. No urinary catheter. Peripheral IV to be removed before departure.

**SNF Orders**
- PT and OT daily; weight bearing as tolerated right leg; fall precautions; walker.
- Ceftriaxone 1 g IM daily (next dose tonight 2330, third dose Thursday); final agent and duration per the culture. Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily through 12/13 (35 days).
- Labs Friday 11/13: BMP and CBC. Restart metformin after the BMP if creatinine stable; resume alendronate when upright 30 minutes.
- Diet: consistent-carbohydrate, 2 g sodium with protein supplement BID; encourage fluids 1,500 mL/day.
- Monitor for recurrent fever, confusion, urinary retention; bladder scan if no void in 6 hours.
- Keep Aquacel dressing until follow-up.

**Follow-up**
Dr. Reyes (Orthopedics) in 2 weeks for staple removal and x-ray. PCP after SNF discharge. Karen Mills present and updated.

title: Case Management Transfer Note
author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
summary: Transfer to Maple Grove arranged for 1430 by wheelchair van; nurse-to-nurse report at 1330, paperwork and insurance complete.
body:
**Transfer Plan**
Patient is cleared by Dr. Patel for transfer to Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation today.

- Transport: wheelchair van booked for pickup at 1430 from the 4 West unit.
- Nurse-to-nurse report: scheduled for 1330, bedside nurse L. Okoye, RN to C. Pruitt, RN (Maple Grove).
- Family: daughter Karen Mills will be present and will follow the van in her car. She has the patient's glasses, left hearing aid, cane, clothes and shoes. Belongings were checked against the list.

**Paperwork Sent to the Facility**
- Discharge/transfer summary (Dr. Patel), medication reconciliation (A. Chen, PharmD), orders and the MAR, PT and OT notes.
- Allergy list (sulfa), code status (Full Code), health care proxy information.
- Controlled-substance prescription for oxycodone and the enoxaparin and ceftriaxone doses due.
- Pending culture results and how to follow them; follow-up appointment with Dr. Reyes in 2 weeks (orthopedic office will call to schedule).

**Insurance**
Medicare Part A skilled nursing benefit; qualifying 3-midnight inpatient stay met. No prior authorization needed. Reviewed the cost-sharing information with Karen.

**Patient / Family**
Patient agrees with the plan and states she is ready to start rehabilitation. Karen has no concerns. Education provided on what to expect at the SNF, goals for returning home, and that PT/OT will be daily.

**Follow-up**
Will confirm arrival with Maple Grove after transfer and be available to the facility for questions. Home needs (raised toilet seat, shower chair) to be addressed before discharge from the SNF.
